overview_markdown:
LettaBot is a personal AI assistant built on the Letta platform that connects a single stateful agent to Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, and Signal, with read-only Bluesky Jetstream feed ingestion. Its standout feature is unified persistent memory: one agent remembers conversations across all channels and across sessions spanning days or months, powered by the Letta Code SDK. It also supports local tool execution (file reads, code search, shell commands), voice message transcription via OpenAI Whisper, heartbeat check-ins, and agent-created scheduled reminders.

Architecturally, it is a Node.js/TypeScript application that requires either a Letta cloud API key or a self-hosted Letta Docker server, making it dependent on the Letta backend rather than fully local-first. Configuration is YAML-driven, and a Railway one-click deploy template lowers the barrier for always-on hosting.

Critically, LettaBot is **officially deprecated**. The maintainers have archived the project and direct all new development to Letta Code's Channels (for messaging integrations) and Remote Environments (for always-on agents via outbound WebSocket). Existing deployments continue to function, and migration is described as taking roughly 20 minutes, but anyone evaluating OpenClaw alternatives should treat this as a legacy reference implementation rather than a going concern.
